section_03.text_001: Delivery is not the end of usability.
section_03.text_002: A handover can contain every promised file and still be difficult to use. If the next person has to search through a message history to understand which version is final, the work is technically present but practically incomplete.
section_03.text_004: Think about what the next team needs to do. A developer needs relevant files and implementation context. A client needs a clear way to find final assets. A future project manager needs to understand decisions and outstanding responsibilities.
section_03.text_006: Use plain labels, group related assets, and connect each link to its purpose. “Final presentation template” is more useful than “Updated file 7.” Explain permissions or usage details where they are necessary.
section_03.text_007: Be honest about what is open.
section_03.text_008: A useful handover distinguishes finished work from decisions or inputs still outstanding. It names the person responsible for each remaining step. A tidy document should not hide an unresolved dependency.
section_03.text_010: Imagine opening the handover without having attended any project meetings. Can you find the final files? Can you understand the immediate next step? Can you tell who to contact? If those answers are easy, the handover is doing its job.
